text:
max: quick proposal — move prompt/user-id/request-id hashing + coarse bucketing into the aggregator (before exporter). reason: reduce high-cardinality churn at downstream exporters/storage and make retention cheaper. :thinking:
sara: curious — aggregator does more work but can we still preserve debugability? if we hash request_id upstream we lose ability to correlate full traces across services unless we keep a lookup for authorized SRE flows
jon: +1 on cost side. concern: if aggregator does hashing, we need deterministic salt rotation plan so dashboards don't explode on salt changes
mike: what about differential redaction levels: keep full request_id for internal-only spans but scrub for external exporters? that lets us debug internally, keeps customer-facing traces safe
lina: read-only lookup sounds scary for compliance. audit logs need to know when/why a raw id was used. storing mappings increases risk and KMS complexity
max: thought about a tiered approach: 1) ingest-level tokenization for non-PII attrs (prompt_hash, user_bucket) 2) keep an ephemeral mapping accessible only to oncall for 30d 3) exporters receive only bucketed attrs and hashed ids
sara: UX concern: our console rollups (per-route latency, prompt-regression alerts) rely on prompt_hash continuity. any salt rotation must be smooth or we get duplicated series. need a migration/rollout plan + UI note
jon: technical sketch: aggregator will run small consistent-hash function: sha256(id + rotation_epoch) -> hex -> take first 8 chars. rotation_epoch increments monthly. store rotation_epoch in trace attributes so we can re-hash on query for internal debug
mike: code snippet for aggregator hook we discussed:

```
// aggregator middleware
attr = span.attributes
if (attr.prompt) {
  attr.prompt_hash = sha256_salted(attr.prompt, current_epoch)[:8]
  delete attr.prompt
}
if (attr.request_id) {
  attr.rid_hash = sha256_salted(attr.request_id, current_epoch)[:8]
  // optionally drop raw request_id
}
export(span)
```

lina: where do exporters put this? otel semantic conventions expect stable keys. we should name keys explicitly: telemetry.redwood.prompt_hash, telemetry.redwood.rid_hash. avoid using generic request_id which folks may assume raw value
telemetry-bot: Note: sampling policy change scheduled by eng-platform on 2026-07-01. Will apply to traces from aggregator stage onward.
max: perf numbers: prototype aggregator hashing adds ~0.4ms/span CPU on p100 workload, but reduces unique-value cardinality to storage by ~87% in our test corpus. promising but need long-term retention effects
sara: also think about quotas: if we aggressively bucket prompts, cost per-query drops but customers might see less granular breakdowns in cost dashboards. we should add a flag that shows "estimated unique prompts" vs "raw prompts" in the console
jon: about debugging: propose a short-lived HMAC-encrypted mapping service for SRE: store <hashed, encrypted_raw> for 7 days, require ticket + audit to decrypt. reduces blast radius vs full mapping store
mike: encryption + RBAC is fine but increases infra surface area. We should measure how often SRE needs raw prompt vs hashed — maybe <1% of incidents. If so, keep it as an opt-in debug path behind feature flag
max: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag aggregator hashing in canary clusters -> collect metrics: incidents requiring raw prompts, dashboard continuity, cardinality drop -> if stable, flip in 2 regions -> rotate salt once after 30d -> observe
sara: one more: telemetry retention interplay. If we only keep ephemeral mapping for 7d but retention for spans is 90d, we won't be able to get raw for older traces. is that OK for postmortems? maybe allow longer retention for fodder traces under enterprise contracts
lina: legal/compliance: for EU customers who opt-out of any personal identifiers we must ensure aggregator-scrub happens inside customer VPC or private deployment. public hosted can't claim to do EU-pseudonymization without tenant isolation
jon: operational hooks: add metric exporter for "hashing_rate", "mapping_lookups", "mapping_miss_rate" so we know how often teams request raw values and whether mapping cache works
mike: and add dashboard card in Console: "Telemetry scrubbing impact" with time-series for unique prompt counts pre/post-scrub, errors in evals, and number of SRE decrypt requests
max: ok next steps: 1) I'll open a design doc with the deterministic-salt + mapping-service + exporter keynames 2) sara / lina to add console/ compliance requirements 3) jon to prototype aggregator middleware 4) mike to add metrics + flags
sara: thumbs up. can we also add a UX note for rollouts: when salt rotates show a banner "metric series may fragment during rotation window" with link to migration guide
telemetry-bot: Action: design doc created at https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry/aggregator-scrub-proposal - assigned: max, jon, sara. Due: 2026-06-10
max: thanks — will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
